runs.t: •  Ask and answer Have you… yet?

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive.
Point to the title and read it: "Have you finished yet?" Say: "Tonight we talk about work: what is done, what is not done yet, and a short check-in with a supervisor."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "I've already clocked in." • "Have you cleaned the break room yet? No, not yet." • "What have you done this week?"
Keep work talk positive and invented. Learners never discuss real problems with real bosses or coworkers. Any job works in the role plays; invented answers are fine.
Lesson plan: Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Teacher notes.

slides.title: Have You Finished Yet?

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these five things.
Every goal is a good goal.
I can say what I've already done and what I've just done.
Yes, I've already… / No, not yet.
I can answer a supervisor's check-in questions in 3 sentences.
I can write a reply email (5–8 sentences) about what is done and not done yet.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: I've already restocked the shelves. I've just cleaned the board. Goal 2: Have you clocked in yet? Yes, I've already clocked in. / No, not yet. Goal 3: already and just before the past participle; yet at the end.
Goal 4: the Check-in in Talk Time. Goal 5: the reply email in Read & Write (Writing Check 1).
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives.

slides.notes:
Step 1 · 6:00–6:08 · Opening Talk + Homework Check · 8 min. Pairs (7 pairs + 1 trio with 15 learners; 3–4 pairs with 7–8).
Before class, write on the board: How long have you…? and for / since
Model with one learner: you ask, "How long have you lived in this city?" The learner answers with for or since. Then you ask, "Where did you live before? How long did you live there?" Help them say 3 sentences. (Click to show the follow-up.)
Opening Talk (5 min): learners open the Opening Talk page. A asks a card question; B answers in 3 sentences (the answer, a reason, a detail); A asks one follow-up. Switch after each card. The cards are on the next slide.
If behind: one card only.

runs.t: B answers in 3 sentences: the answer, a reason, and a detail.
When did you…? Where did you… before? Why?
How long have you lived in this city?
How long have you had your phone?
How long have you known your best friend?
How long have you studied English?

slides.notes:
Step 1, continued. The four cards from the Opening Talk page. Each click shows the next card.
A asks a card question. B answers in 3 sentences. A asks one follow-up question (follow-ups on the right). Then switch. Pairs write the partner's name and one How long…? answer (for / since).
Homework Check (3 min, last click): pairs compare Homework item 1 (for / since sentences) and read one answer from item 3 to each other. Then they fill in the box on the Opening Talk page. Walk around. Write 2 common errors on the board (often I live here since 2020 (→ I've lived here since 2020) and since three years (→ for three years)) and correct them together. Also put up 2 corrections from last week's exit tickets.

slides.notes:
Step 3 · 6:15–6:30 · Listening + "Hear it, say it" · 15 min (slides 8 to 12). Individuals, then pairs check.
Before you listen (2 min). Say: "It's the end of the evening shift at a grocery store. Ms. Rivera, the supervisor, talks to two workers, Jamal and Kim. Listen: is all the work finished?"
There are three people: Ms. Rivera (the supervisor), Jamal, and Kim. A narrator starts and ends the listening. Each click highlights the next person.
The audio (L4_L3_listening.mp3, about 1:59) plays the conversation once. Press play again for play 2. A third play is fine if the class needs it.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer at a natural, friendly speed, two times. The script says going to and want to. People often say gonna and wanna; learners only need to recognize those words.
Audio: synthetic voices, computer-generated (Chatterbox TTS cloned from Kokoro-82M reference clips). No recordings of real people. The names and the story are invented.

slides.title: Listening C

runs.t: Hear it: gonna = going to, wanna = want to
Say it: 's = has, and the stress
are short forms. This listening uses the full forms.
clean it before I clock out.

slides.notes:
"Hear it, say it" (3 min). Point to the script lines. gonna = going to: "I'm going to clean it before I clock out." wanna = want to: "I want to finish it this week." You can say going to and want to.
Then practice hearing 's = has: It's just arrived (= it has just arrived), the weak have in Have you… yet?, and the stress: I've JUST finished it. • I've alREADY restocked them. The class repeats the two lines twice.
's = has: It's just arrived. She's already left. Ask: "is or has?" If a past participle comes next, it is has.
Lesson plan: Step 3: "Hear it, say it"; Listening page: Hear it, say it; Teacher notes.

slides.title: already / yet / just

shapes.name: pic
shapes.alt: Task: a broom and a sponge [sign: TASK: CLEAN]

slides.notes:
Box 2: add a time → simple past: I finished them at 3:00. Each click shows the answer side of one row.
Rule of thumb (read it aloud): already = done (maybe sooner than expected). yet = in questions and not sentences, at the end. just = a very short time ago. Add a time (at 3:00, yesterday) → simple past.

runs.t: I've finished the orders. I haven't called her yet.

slides.notes:
Box 4: which one? Each click shows one row.
Questions and answers (2 min): Q: Can I say I've finished it yesterday? A: No. With a finished time, use the simple past: I finished it yesterday. • Q: Where does yet go? A: At the end: Have you clocked out yet? I haven't clocked out yet. • Q: What does It's just arrived mean? A: It's = it has. just = a very short time ago. The truck arrived a minute ago.
Check questions: "I've finished it yesterday. Right or wrong?" (wrong: I finished it yesterday.) • "Where does yet go?" (at the end) • "It's just arrived. It's = it is or it has?" (it has).

runs.t: A looks at Card A. B covers it.
Yes, I've already restocked it. / No, not yet.
B ticks done or not yet. Then switch.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:15 · Talk Time: Shift Handoff + Check-in · 15 min.
Model it first (1 min): hold up Card A and ask a learner to ask you, "Have you restocked aisle 3 yet?" Answer, "Yes, I've already restocked it." Then point to a task with no tick: "No, not yet. I'm going to do it before I clock out." Say: "Answer, then add one more sentence."
Round 1 (7 min): Shift Handoff (pairs, information gap). A looks at Card A; B covers it. B asks Have you… yet? about each task and ticks done or not yet in the notes. Then switch: A asks about Card B. Each click shows the next step.
15 learners: pairs for round 1. 7–8 learners: pairs for round 1. 5 or fewer: pairs (or one group of 3) for round 1.
Keep work talk positive and invented. Learners never discuss real problems with real bosses or coworkers. Any job works in the role plays; invented answers are fine.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time: Shift Handoff; Teacher notes.

shapes.name: pic
shapes.alt: Check-in (a short meeting): a supervisor and a worker talking

runs.t: A supervisor, a worker, an observer.
What have you done this week?
The observer ticks the words. Then rotate.

slides.notes:
Round 2 (6 min): Check-in (groups of 3). The supervisor reads the 3 question cards. The worker answers with already and yet (invented answers are fine). The observer ticks each already / yet / just they hear. Rotate roles so everyone is the worker once. Each click shows the next step.
Question cards: 1. What have you done this week? 2. Have you finished the training yet? 3. What's one thing you'd like to learn? Useful (supervisor): Great job! • Thanks for your hard work. • When are you going to finish it? • Let me know if you need help.
Example (worker): "This week I've already restocked the drinks aisle, and I've trained a new coworker. I haven't finished the safety training yet. I'm going to do it on Thursday because the deadline is Friday."
15 learners: 5 groups of 3. 7–8 learners: 2 groups (the group of 4 has two workers). 5 or fewer: you play the supervisor first; then learners take turns.
Every answer needs a reason; every partner asks a follow-up. Walk around and listen. Note 2 good sentences to praise and 1 common error for next week.
If behind: round 1 only.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time: Check-in.

runs.t: What is the deadline for the safety training?
Where can workers do the training?
On the computer in the break room.

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:15–7:25 · Read & Write: An email from a supervisor + a reply · 10 min. Pairs read, then individual writing.
Read (4 min): learners read the email from Sandra on the Read & Write page and answer the questions. Say: "Read fast first. Then find the answers." Pairs answer questions 1–5 together.
Check (1 min): click to show each answer (one click per question, 1 to 5): 1 The evening team. • 2 By Thursday. • 3 Friday, May 16. • 4 On the computer in the break room. • 5 The new schedule.
Write (5 min): learners write a reply email (5–8 sentences): what they've already done, what they haven't done yet, when they'll finish it, and one question. Show the example. Invented details are fine. This is Writing Check 1: collect it. Learners start in class and finish at home (Homework item 2).
Writing Check 1: collect the reply emails. Write one strength and one fix on each (for example, the place of yet). Return them next week; learners keep them in a folder to see progress. No scores.
If behind: questions 1–5 only; the writing becomes homework.
Lesson plan: Step 6; Read & Write page; Answer key; Teacher notes: Writing Check 1.
slides.title: Read & Write

shapes.name: pic
shapes.alt: To-do list: a note and a pencil [sign: TO DO]

runs.t: Give it to me at the door.
1. Write the sentence. Use the words.
2. Finish your reply email (Read & Write C).
3. Make a to-do list for this week.

slides.notes:
Step 7 · 7:25–7:30 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket (3 min): learners open the Exit Ticket page and answer in 3 sentences with a reason: What have you done this week, and what haven't you done yet? Example on the board: I've already paid my phone bill. I haven't done my laundry yet. I haven't done it because I worked late every night. With 5 or fewer, a learner can say it to you first and then write it.
Collect the pages. After class, sort them into ✓ / almost / not yet. Start next week with 2 corrections on the board (no names).
Homework (2 min): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (you / finish / the checklist / yet? → Have you finished the checklist yet?). Say: "About 15–20 minutes. Finish your Read & Write writing at home."
Homework items: 1 write the sentence with the words • 2 finish the reply email from Read & Write C and check it with the list in D • 3 make a to-do list for this week: 3 things you've already done and 2 things you haven't done yet • 4 review (object pronouns): it or them.
Lesson plan: Step 7; Exit Ticket page; Homework page.
